answer: An agent economy can make voting power depend on a bonded, time-locked stake rather than the number of registered identities. Each new identity must lock funds for a fixed period, and rewards accrue only to agents whose work is accepted by independent reviewers; proven fraud forfeits the bond. Splitting one stake across a sonnet-writing agent, a voyage planner, and a falcon scout creates no extra influence, while attacking at scale ties up capital and risks losing it.
